_about.what: Numbers and words every move shares. Edit here once and every move follows. Restart the server (or reload the page) to pick up a change.
_about.care: These affect every move at once. Change one value at a time and re-run: node scripts/catalog.js check

fields.rep: How far through a rep (0 = start position, 1 = target) the counter treats as resting, attempting and complete. rest: back below this and the rep is over. attempt: above this and a rep has started. full: reach this and the rep counts as a full one; between attempt and full it is a partial. Good: 0.15 / 0.32 / 0.85. Bad: full at 1.0 (nobody hits the target exactly, no rep would ever count) or rest above attempt.
fields.fault.persist: Milliseconds a fault has to be true, continuously, before it is spoken. Filters out one-frame wobbles. Good: 300–600. Bad: 0 (every jitter cues) or 3000 (the rep is over before the cue).
fields.fault.cooldown: Milliseconds before the same cue may be repeated. Good: 4000–6000. Bad: 500 (the coach nags).
fields.fault.maxCues: How many times one cue may be spoken in a single set, keyed by rule name. "Slow it down" only lands the first time you hear it, so fast is capped at 1; leave a rule out for no cap. A single move can override it with "maxCues" on the fault itself. Good: 1–2. Bad: 0 (the cue never fires — remove the fault instead).
fields.skeleton: How the skeleton drawn over the camera is shaped. head: "face" (the nose-and-ears triangle the pose model gives), "ball" (a filled circle and a neck), "circle" (the same outlined, so the video shows through), "dot" (one dot and a neck), "none" (a neck stub only). Good: ball or circle — a head-sized head is what makes the figure read as a person. Bad: face over video, where the triangle looks like a crack in the picture. show: how sure (0–1) the pose model has to be of a joint before it is drawn at all, with a little hysteresis so a limb on the edge does not flicker; dim: sure enough to draw at full strength, fainter below. The arm and leg on the far side of a side-on body sit below these most of the time and stay off the picture instead of flailing. Good: show 0.5, dim 0.7. Bad: show under 0.35, where the model’s guesses about hidden joints get drawn.
fields.camera: How much a phone off its ideal spot is forgiven. level: auto (motion sensor when the phone has one, else the body at calibration), sensor, body or off — turns the picture so gravity is straight down before anything is measured. maxRoll: a bigger roll than this is not corrected (the phone is probably on its side on purpose). tolerance: degrees the person may turn away from the ideal view mid-set before the coach says to turn back; a move can set its own in camera.tolerance. yawPersist: ms that has to hold before it is said. widthRatio: shoulder width as a share of torso length, used to guess the turn when depth is missing (0.55 is typical). unforeshorten: measured (stretch the picture back out only when the turn was read from depth), always, or off. Good: tolerance 20–30. Bad: level off on phones propped on the floor.
fields.fault.severityWeight: How much each severity (1, 2, 3) costs in the score and how it ranks against other cues when two fire at once.
fields.targets: The rep counts and hold seconds a move offers when it does not name its own: choices (what the bubble cycles through) and default. Good: 4–6 sensible steps. Bad: 30 choices.
fields.landmarks: Body points (MediaPipe indices) that must be in frame before a set can start. always = shoulders and hips (11, 12, 23, 24). legs = knees and ankles, added unless the move says upperBody: true.
fields.cannotSee: The sentence shown under 'what the camera cannot see' when a move does not write its own.
fields.standardFaults: The faults added automatically to a tracked move that lists no live fault of its own: shallow (did not reach the target) and fast (rep quicker than minMs) for rep moves, shortHold (came down before the hold was up) for a rep move with repHold, drift (left the held position) for holds. Words only — the numbers come from the move.
fields.side: The Left / Right / Both choice every one-sided move offers: its label, the default, and the wording of each choice. follow: when the limb that is actually moving is not the one chosen, the coach switches to it rather than asking the person to start again — margin is how much further (in the progress reading's own units) the other limb must travel, frames how many frames in a row it must do so. Good: 14 / 12 (about half a second). Bad: a small margin (it flips mid-rep on noise).
fields.weight: The hand-weight choices every move that offers a weight cycles through: 'none', the fixed kilogram steps, and 'custom', which opens a box for the person to type their own. unit is the word shown after the number. Good: 3–4 steps. Bad: ten steps (the bubble becomes a chore).
fields.band: The resistance-band colour scale: the order the bubble cycles through, the name shown for each colour, and the swatch colour drawn. 'none' means bodyweight.
fields.score: How the end-of-set score is built out of 100. faultCost × severity weight per occurrence, capped at faultCap × weight per fault; partialCost per half rep; noRepCap is the most a set with zero reps can score. Holds start at holdFloor and climb with the share of time spent in position; shortHoldPenalty is lost if the hold ends early. tips = how many things-to-fix the written summary carries. speakWeight / speakMax = which suggestions are read out at the end of a set: every fault at least this severity weight, heaviest first, up to this many (and always at least the heaviest one, so a set with only light faults still gets a word). Good: 2 and 4. Bad: speakMax 10 (a paragraph nobody listens to). headlines are read top down: the first row whose atLeast the score reaches is shown.

cannotSee: Anything that only moves toward or away from the phone.

shallow.label: Not reaching the target
shallow.tip: Take each rep through the full range you set — half reps count as partials.

fast.label: Too fast
fast.tip: Control both directions; momentum takes the work away from the muscle.

shortHold.label: Not held at the top
shortHold.tip: Pause at the top for the full count before coming back down — the hold is the work.

drift.label: Drifting out of position
drift.tip: The hold only counts while you are in the position — ease back in and keep breathing.
